entities.summary: Giuseppe Ambrosoli was an Italian Catholic priest and professed member from the Comboni Missionaries of the Heart of Jesus. He served as a doctor and surgeon as well as being a philanthropist and educator in the missions in Uganda. Ambrosoli studied before World War II when he once risked his life to smuggle Jewish people into Switzerland before returning home to finish his studies in medicine prior to commencing his ecclesial studies. He joined the Comboni missionaries and was sent to Uganda where he became known as the "saint doctor" for his loving and compassionate treatment of all ill people whom he dedicated himself to.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Giuseppe Ambrosoli's work as a doctor and surgeon in Uganda during the colonial era had a significant impact on the local healthcare system, with his compassionate treatment of patients earning him the nickname "saint doctor." His philanthropic efforts also contributed to the development of education and community services in the region.
